description: Use for the history, rules, source and proof of one index named by list_indices (LAYOFFS, YESNO, TRENCHES, MINTS, GIGS, WAGE, JOBS, UNEMP, CPI, CORECPI). JOBS, UNEMP, CPI and CORECPI are monthly, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics: a day's value is the Bureau's figure now, its settlement_value is the first print Tickerz read at release, and a month loaded as history carries a note and no settlement_value. One Tickerz Index: its definition, every period in its read window with its band and signed z, the first print of the newest complete period, the open round, past rounds, and the newest proof. latest_complete is the finished period; a provisional latest is a partial UTC day (partial_day true), and its change_pct, also given as partial_change_pct, is not a full-day change. WAGE days, latest and latest_complete carry p25 and p75 where the store has them. GIGS and WAGE complete days carry thin and sampled_payers: thin is true when sampled paying wallets are under 70% of the median of the 28 complete days before that day, once 14 earlier days are on file, and the level stays. Fewer earlier days is not marked. For what is on-chain, read proof: covers_period and covers_value are the newest period of this index a proof holds and its value there, stamped_on is the UTC day that proof was stamped, with digest_sha256, bitcoin_height, proof_url (the exact text hashed, as JSON) and ots_url (the OpenTimestamps file), status (on_chain, awaiting_bitcoin, none or unavailable), and latest_complete with on_chain true or false. A live source's day is complete at 00:00 UTC and goes on-chain in the next day's proof, stamped after 12:00 UTC, so stamped_on is a day after covers_period and the newest complete day is often not on-chain yet. seal is the newest daily proof for every index: seal.day is the day it was stamped, not a period of this index. first_print is for latest_complete and stays null until a proof holds it. forecast is Forecast v1 for the next period: p10, p50 and p90 (an 80% range and its middle), the model the daily run chose, backtest (periods walked forward, coverage_80, skill_vs_last_number: the share of error removed against repeating the last number, negative when worse) and the live record; display only, never a settled number, null when none. Same data as GET /api/indices/{ticker}, plus proof. Levels a source's terms keep out of the API are null.
